56e967b74c71f00005d78743.housing_experience: Before COVID, I had a two-bedroom home that I was renting.   This home had a nice fenced in backyard.   I had a two-car garage, and more space in the driveway.    I was in the cul-de-sac so I had lots of area for my daughter to run around and play.    We were within close walking distance to her school, which was one of the best rated in the state.    We had a fully functional kitchen, living room, bathroom, and laundry room.   The house was in no way updated as far as the way it looked, but it was very livable.    The neighborhood was old, and full of lower working class families.    I was paying $800 a month, and around $150 a month for utilities.    Then came COVID.   The owners of the house decided to sell, because they had multiple mortgages for multiple homes that they had purchased in 2008.   They both were making good money, but with two of their rental homes sitting empty, and no prospects to move in, they took the home that needed the most work, and put it on the market.    Because it wasn't an expensive place, it sold almost immediately, and I was out a home.    I decided to head to Puerto Rico for a little bit.    I just needed a change of pace for a few months while I decided what was next.   Is there anything after this?   I stayed in PR for about 6 months, and then came back home.    Upon my return, those homes in that same neighborhood were now $1800, but you know what didn't change?   How much I was making.    How can you now charge double for a home in a neighborhood in 6 months?   What changed?
